title: UGANDA: Bishop Calls on Christians to Reject Modern Idols and Put God First for Peace
desc:
Fr. Isaac Ojok
The Bishop of Arua diocese in North Western Uganda, Rt. Rev. Sabino Ochan Odoki, has called on Christians to reject modern-day idols and embrace God as the foundation for lasting peace in society.
Bishop Odoki made the appeal during the closing Eucharistic celebration of the provincial Prayer and peace Week held at Lango College, in Lira diocese where he presided over the final Mass commissioning peace pilgrims to return to their respective dioceses as ambassadors of peace.
The Prayer Peace Week has been taking place in Lira diocese under the theme, “Peace Be With You” drawn from John 20:19. The week-long pastoral and spiritual gathering attracted participants from the four dioceses under the Gulu Ecclesiastical Province, namely Gulu Archdiocese, Lira diocese, Nebbi catholic diocese, and Arua diocese including Kotido in North Eastern Uganda.
In his homily, Bishop Odoki warned that many people today have allowed worldly distractions to take the place of God in their lives, something he said continues to deprive society of genuine peace.
“Idols take away our minds from the true God. God becomes secondary while other things take priority in our lives,” the bishop said.
He listed money, wealth, political and economic power, social media, artificial intelligence, prestige, excessive pursuit of comfort, alcohol abuse, and obsession with physical appearance as some of the modern idols affecting society today.
The bishop particularly criticized the growing tendency among some people to prioritize outward appearance over spiritual values.
“People are changing their color, spending resources on appearances and forgetting God,” he said, adding that even within the Church, the struggle for positions and authority can become an idol when people seek offices for personal glory instead of service.
Bishop Odoki noted that peace can only flourish where people put God first and live according to the gifts and fruits of the Holy Spirit.
“The gift of the Holy Spirit should help us to promote peace. If peace is becoming a challenge, then it means we are not putting the fruits of the Holy Spirit into practice,” he said.
The bishop explained that the Eucharistic celebration marked the commissioning of peace pilgrims to go out as messengers of peace to the world. He said the Mass of the Holy Spirit was intentionally chosen so that the Spirit of God may accompany the mission of peace entrusted to all participants.
Reflecting on the state of the country, Bishop Odoki observed that many people lack inner peace and are living with growing discontent.
“We need to understand peace as a gift from God which we must carry back home to our dioceses and communities,” he emphasized.
He reminded Christians that at creation God breathed His Spirit into humanity and that through Baptism believers receive the Holy Spirit whose gifts bear fruits such as charity, peace, patience, kindness, self-control, modesty, and chastity.
The bishop also encouraged Ugandans to promote dialogue, respect human rights, uphold democratic values, and reject violence in order to build peaceful communities.
He further urged Christians to fight corruption, tribalism, favoritism, laziness, and poverty, saying such vices continue to undermine harmony and development in society.
Citing the Gospel reading of the day, Bishop Odoki said Jesus commands believers to love one another, noting that love remains the foundation of every peaceful society.
Quoting the theological virtues of faith, hope, and love as taught by St Paul, the Bishop stressed that love is the greatest and the basis of all human relationships.
Earlier at the start of the Eucharistic celebratiom, Bishop Odoki welcomed pilgrims and guests, thanking God for sustaining participants throughout the Prayer peace Week. He expressed gratitude to the bishop, clergy, and faithful of Lira diocese for their hospitality and appreciated the administration of Lango College, the host venue for providing a conducive environment for the event.
He also thanked all individuals and leaders who contributed towards the success of the function, including government officials and supporters who offered financial and moral support to the bishops’ ministry and the peace initiative.
The bishop while flanked by other bishops of the province concluded by blessing the peace pilgrims, their families, and the nation of Uganda, urging all participants to return home as missionaries of peace and put into practice the knowledge gained during the week-long gathering.
End.
